searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, three left unspent. The three shared searches went to the law of 18 September 1908 and the decree of 25 May 1910 (the CCDR Centro and Decree Law 376/93 by FAOLEX), to the CVR Dão's own account of the co-operatives, and to the origin of Touriga Nacional. The houses' own domains were searched by restriction six times (quintaroques.pt three times, quintadapellada.com, sogrape.com, casadesantar.pt), each read as primary through its summary, and the consolidated portaria through its summary on the Diário da República; the rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked (Raymond Reynolds, Fareham, Wine House Portugal, The Wine Society, Center of Portugal, Wine Paris, Oleobrigado, En Primeur Club, Evaton, Liberty Wines, Loja do Vinho, Drinkfinder, Essential Algarve, Cave Lusa, Portugal Get Wine and, where the account had to be independent, the house itself). No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the law and the rules, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own pages for their own dates and methods (three of the five houses' pages the author had not reached: the Roques sheets, the Pellada history, the Santar legend), then to independent accounts of each house's history, then to merchants' sheets of each wine with the author's sources blocked, and to the governing texts for the Dão and the mention Reserva.

Where the sheets disagreed and none was primary, the figure was widened or hedged; where a fact rested on one account and the refuter found it nowhere (hand picking at Passarella, Primus from one high parcel, a claim made for Sogrape of renewing the region, a fifth of the Roques Encruzado in oak), it was taken out or corrected to the house's own sheet.

tested: The founding and the dates, the author's merchants and importer blocked: the house's own About page, searched on its domain, gives roots in the nineteenth century, the hamlet of Abrunhosa do Mato between Mangualde and Nelas, varietal reds from 1996, Touriga Nacional among them, an Encruzado made alone from 1998, and varietal wines made only when the house judges the quality good enough. Borne out, now on the house itself rather than its importer.

The making of the Touriga Nacional: the house's 2019 sheet gives wholly destemmed grapes fermented in stainless steel at 28 to 30 degrees with some thirteen days of maceration, fourteen months in 225 litre French oak and a light filtration, served at 16 degrees. The author's well over a year stands, the fifteen to seventeen months of the merchants widens to fourteen to seventeen.

The sites: the house's page gives granite and, at times, schist on gentle south facing slopes; a writer's profile (read, not cited) gives mostly granitic sand with a little schist and clay at about 450 metres, the figure the author took from two merchants. The 450 metres stands on three accounts, none of them the house; the soils were widened.

The Encruzado in others: the house's sheets of 2017, 2019 and 2022 give half the wine fermented in French oak barrels (500 litres in 2022) for six or seven months with the lees stirred twice a week and half in steel, with selected yeasts in 2022. The author's fifth in oak with its own yeasts was not borne out.

Quinta das Maias: Fareham's listing names it Gouveia, Decanter files it under the Serra da Estrela subregion, and the accounts read put it higher than Roques at about 600 metres, bought by the family in 1997 by a writer's profile and The Wine Society. The note in others stands; the story's holds, a present ownership, became took on, with no year.

The law of 18 September 1908 and the decree of 25 May 1910: the CCDR Centro and Decree Law 376/93 by FAOLEX. The co-operatives of the 1960s and 1970s: the CVR Dão's own page. Touriga Nacional said to be born in the Dão: Falstaff and the accounts read give it as the prevailing view on DNA evidence, the Douro also claiming it, so the hedge stands.
The house rules: nobody living named (the family and its son in law are never named), no price, no score, nothing volatile once holds became took on, no judging superlative, British, no dash.

changed.was: Made from the estate's Touriga Nacional alone, fermented on its skins and then aged for well over a year in French oak barrels before bottling. The merchants' sheets give fifteen to seventeen months, in used barrels for some vintages and new ones for others.
changed.now: Made only in years the house judges good enough: the grapes are wholly destemmed and fermented on their skins in stainless steel vats, then the wine is aged for fourteen to seventeen months, by vintage, in 225 litre French oak barrels, new in some years and used in others, and lightly filtered before bottling.
changed.why: The house's own 2019 sheet gives the destemming, the steel, fourteen months in 225 litre French oak and the light filtration; its About page makes the varietal wines only in years it judges good enough; Fareham gives seventeen months in new barrels.

tested: The history, the author's sources blocked: the estate's own history page, which the author did not find, gives the first records in 1527, a royal tax of eighty barrels of wine, a civil engineer of the family who inherited in 1980 and revived a tradition lapsed for a generation; Clube de Vinhos Portugueses and two guides give about 1570 for the first records and the first label, Quinta de Saes, with the 1989 vintage. Borne out: the record of 1527 is the house's own, the sixteenth century the hedge, the 1980 inheriting now primary.

The place: the estate's terroir page sets its vineyards at 450 to 600 metres on granite in the Serra da Estrela subregion and names Vila Nova de Tazém nearby; Clube de Vinhos Portugueses and two guides give Pinhanços, Seia. The place stands.

Carrocel, the author's merchants blocked: Leon and Son, Vivino and Mistral give Touriga Nacional alone from a single parcel of about half a hectare at about 500 metres on granite, planted in 1950; fermentation in stainless steel with up to twelve days of maceration on three sheets; 24 months in used 400 litre French oak (Leon and Son), 30 months in 400 litre casks of two or three years (Mistral), about two years (Vinogrande); made only in the strong vintages by Garrafeira Nacional. Borne out, with the steel fermentation now on three sheets.

Primus: Vinogrande, Mistral and Cave Lusa give a field blend of old vines led by Encruzado and Bical with Cerceal, Terrantez, Malvasia Fina and others planted among them, the musts fermented together. The author's one high parcel was not borne out.

Pape and Doda, for the library: Doda, called Dado from the 2000 to the 2004 vintage, is the Douro and Dão blend made with the Douro house; Pape is a red of Quinta da Pellada alone. The author's reading stands, and the library's line is reported.
The house rules: the winemaker of the library's producer name, his daughter and the two who joined in 2005 are never named; nothing volatile, British, no dash.

changed.why: The steel fermentation and its twelve days, left out by the author on one source, stand on three sheets read by the refuter.

tested: The dates: Sogrape's Dão page gives the company in the Dão since 1957 and the estate bought and planted in 1988, near Mangualde, its plots growing Touriga Nacional, Alfrocheiro and Encruzado; its Gouveio press note claims the Dão's first Encruzado in 1992. The house's own dates stand; the first is left out, as the author left it.

The making of the Encruzado, the author's sheets and merchants blocked: Garrafeira Portela's 2021 (begun in steel, moved midway into new French oak, about twenty days at up to 19 degrees, about six months in new barrels of various sizes, the rest in steel), Winestuff's 2023 (the same move, about six months in new 225 litre barrels from five coopers, frequent stirring), Continente (seven tenths in new barrels of 225, 500, 1,000 and 2,000 litres for about six months), Gota a Gota's 2021 (four tenths for eight months), Portugal Vineyards's 2018 (fermented in barrels from four coopers, then six months in new oak). The share and the move stand; the 225 litres alone did not.

Parcela 45: Sogrape's page and two merchants' copies of its note give the fire of 15 October 2017 at Mangualde, the parcel burnt days after its Alfrocheiro was picked, and the 2017 its last wine. Borne out, with the detail added.

The story's claim that Sogrape, by its own account, helped to renew a region dulled by co-operative rule: not found on the Sogrape pages read; the CVR Dão's own page gives the co-operatives' rule of the 1960s and 1970s, which now carries the sentence.
The house rules: the estate's winemakers and the family that leads Sogrape are never named; nothing volatile, British, no dash.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose, titles or addresses; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json (none of the twelve is there today). Álvaro de Castro is inside the library's producer name for Quinta da Pellada, which people.json allows on that record alone; listing him keeps him out of every other. The long dead of Santar met in the results (the first Conde de Santar of 1904) are not used.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. Each pick is a real house of the Dão with a real wine it is known by, and each now stands on the house's own pages or two sheets: Roques's Touriga Nacional (its varietal of 1996 by its own page), Pellada's Carrocel (the library's old vine flagship, a parcel of old Touriga Nacional on three sheets), Carvalhais's Encruzado (Sogrape's white of the estate), Santar's Reserva (the house's sheet) and Passarella's Villa Oliveira Touriga Nacional (the line of 1893 revived in 2009). The author's four points for the checker are ruled: no first is claimed for Roques or Carvalhais, agreed; the early estate bottling at Santar and its Condessa white are not borne out, agreed, by the refuter's own search as well; the library's Spain and Portugal is wrong and its Pape a Pellada red, while Doda is borne out as the collaboration, reported below; the source title carrying an importer's name is replaced by the house's own page, which carries the 1996 itself.
planNotes: quinta-dos-roques: answered. The varietal Touriga Nacional from the 1996 vintage is on the house's own page (primary), with the Encruzado of 1998; no first is claimed, since Sogrape claims the Dão's first Encruzado in 1992.
